correctness.rationale: For each p<=k, if e=floor(log_p k), the p-factor is product_{j=1}^e (f(p^j)/f(p^{j-1}))^{C_j(n)-1}; j>e contribute exponent zero because at most one interval element has p^j valuation. If p^e divides k+1 all C_j constant; otherwise C_e has a nonempty proper consecutive interval of p^e residues and translation by p^(e-1) changes it, while all smaller C_j are unchanged, and the nonunit adjacent ratio witnesses full p^e least period. CRT independence plus positivity forces any global period to be a period at each prime, so product formula is least period. k=1 and sigma_alpha p-power strictness checked.
